81134.subject: The Attention Bottleneck 🧠
81134.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/anthropic-employment-report

👋 Hey, Linas here! Every day, I break down 3 stories shaping the future of FinTech & Artificial Intelligence - plus the money movements and trends worth tracking. First time here? 400k+ FinTech and AI leaders get this daily. Join them:
Anthropic, the company behind Claude, has just published the most detailed evidence yet of what happens to work when AI agents do most of it. Its October 2026 report, How Employment is Changing at Anthropic, tracks a company where AI agents now log 6 hours for every hour its employees work.
Four numbers stand out:
🚀 Productivity: code commits per engineer rose 5.1x in 6 months, with no rise in code later reverted or deleted.
👥 Hiring: junior roles fell from 27% to 9% of Anthropic’s technical hires.
⏳ Attention: AI agents spend about 80% of their session time idle, waiting on a human.
🧠 Skills: hiring managers now rank judgment and autonomy above domain expertise.
For anyone building or investing in AI, by far the biggest lesson here is that the scarce resource is now human attention and judgment, not labor. And that shift rewrites how AI-native companies should hire, how they should be organized, which AI products will win, and where the returns will go.
One company’s data matters here more than ever because Anthropic is a leading indicator. It works with frontier models before anyone else and has rebuilt its workflows around them, so what happens there is likely to reach AI startups next and the wider economy after. And unlike most future-of-work commentary, this report runs on telemetry, not forecasts: agent logs, code commits, calendars, Slack networks and thousands of hiring scorecards.
We analysed the full 20-page Anthropic report in depth, tested it against our earlier research on Sequoia [ https://substack.com/redirect/a1cef3af-df1d-42e8-9d7c-92ad0275f2dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], a16z [ https://substack.com/redirect/9636516f-0767-4822-b0fc-2738cadb1b26?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] and Claude Code creator Boris Cherny, and turned it into practical, actionable strategy for founders, operators and investors. Inside:
The 12 numbers that matter, in one table, with what each one means for your company
6 strategic insights, from the attention bottleneck to the breaking junior talent pipeline
Where Anthropic’s data backs, and where it contradicts, Sequoia [ https://substack.com/redirect/a1cef3af-df1d-42e8-9d7c-92ad0275f2dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], a16z [ https://substack.com/redirect/9636516f-0767-4822-b0fc-2738cadb1b26?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] and Boris Cherny [ https://substack.com/redirect/cbe98425-975c-41d6-b490-414548d3d4b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], including one finding that cuts against the popular “A

81070.subject: 💰 The Funding: What happens if MSCI drops crypto treasuries like Strategy?
81070.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/c1c9af72-58d8-47c5-88eb-8e5007f7e3dc/unnamed__17_.png?t=1789144554)
Caption: 

Written by Yogita Khatri  | Edited by Zack Abrams

———————————————————————————

Presented By:

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/0f002faa-88b1-4362-8467-fbc25a6c61ee/Screenshot_2026-10-16_at_4.02.56_PM__3___1___1___1_.png?t=1792184177)
Caption: 

———————————————————————————

----------
Happy Sunday, and welcome to the 62nd edition of [The Funding](https://www.theblock.co/newsletters/the-funding)!

MSCI [finalized rules](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-10-15-msci-rules-could-exclude-strategy-mstr-from-indexes-418729) on Oct. 15 that could push Strategy and other crypto treasury companies out of its main global indexes as soon as Nov. 30. What would that mean for how these companies raise money, and is anyone still willing to fund them? I caught up with investors and analysts to find out.

Let's get into it.


----------———————————————————————————

----------
# THE INSIDE VIEW

## What if MSCI drops crypto treasuries?


----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2012e140-bc90-4ae9-b029-9f403353161b/Dat-Image-1200x675.jpg?t=1792371900)
Caption: 

----------
Index provider MSCI recently [approved new rules](https://app2.msci.com/webapp/index_ann/DocGet?pub_key=aq0wbkjxPgo%3D&lang=en&format=html) that target "non-operating" companies, which mainly hold assets instead of running a business, such as digital asset treasury firms, or DATs.

Under the new rules, MSCI will first check whether a company has substantial operating assets, such as equipment or inventory. In the [proposal MSCI published in August](https://www.msci.com/downloads/documents/indexes/consultations/equity/Consultation%20on%20Eligibility%20of%20Non-Operating%20Companies%20for%20the%20%20MSCI%20Global%20Investable%20Market%20Indexes.pdf), that meant operating assets making up more than half of total assets. Companies that fail this check face five financial tests, which in the proposal included whether a company generates operating cash flow and how much it relies on raising capital to buy assets. Those flagged on four or more will be excluded.

Current index members get some leeway: they will be removed only if they fail in both of their two most recent annual filing periods. If they fail in only one, they stay in the index unless they fail the following year. Companies not yet in the index are blocked if they fail in either of the last two years.

In a simulation published in August using May data, MSCI flagged two bitcoin treasury companies, Michael Saylor's Strategy and Japan's Metaplanet, for potential exclusion. Ethereum treasury firm SharpLink
